quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: For routine braking, what should you do?

options.text: Alternate between front and rear brakes to make them last longer.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: A motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Can tip over if you turn too fast.
Is designed to turn at any speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can tip over if you turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Even with three wheels on the ground, a sidecar can tip over if you turn too sharply or go too fast around a corner.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Practice riding on a quiet road.
Flash your lights so others see you.
Practice riding on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on a quiet road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger or heavy load in traffic for the first time, practice on a quiet road. This helps you get used to how your motorcycle handles with the extra weight.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Ride only in the left part of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left part of your lane.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, use your high beam (unless following another vehicle), use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective clothing. Change your lane position as needed to see, be seen, and maintain a safe distance from other traffic.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, they should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Pass one at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider should wait until the first rider has safely returned to the original lane before starting to pass. Continue this pattern until all riders have passed safely.

questions.question: To lower your crash risk, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others and communicate your plans through signals and lane position. Keep a safe distance from other traffic and watch for hazards ahead so you can react quickly.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, you should:

options.text: Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Go faster to exit the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, ease off the throttle and ride straight as you slow down. If you must brake, gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Speed up to increase distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up only increases danger and may cause them to tailgate faster.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time. Brake firmly and do not panic if the brakes lock.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot.
Point in the direction you are changing lanes.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handle grip
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip of a motorcycle. Learn where all your controls are before you ride.

questions.question: A skidding rear tire:

options.text: Eliminates your ability to change direction.
Is only a concern if the front tire is also skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Eliminates your ability to change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a crash. When the rear wheel locks, you cannot change direction. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After at least an hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, within a few minutes after riding starts.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Grip the handlebars tight and speed up to get past the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over grooves or gratings is not dangerous. Relax and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean as the operator leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean when they lean. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator, and hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers see you, especially if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Stay focused on moving through the intersection.
Speed up to make others notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Never assume other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but still do not notice them. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: A person's body gets rid of about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drinks seven drinks in three hours, how many drinks likely remain in their system three hours after their last drink?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: To find how many drinks remain, subtract the hours since the last drink from the total drinks consumed. Example: seven drinks consumed, three hours later means four drinks still in the system.

questions.question: When changing lanes, riders should:

options.text: Rely only on their mirrors to identify other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Slam on the brakes to allow vehicles in their blind spot to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: Maximum straight-line braking is done by:

options.text: Using both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel.
Using both the front and rear brakes while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: To stop in the shortest distance on a straight road, use both brakes without locking either wheel.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
Increase your ability to be seen by others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: Good lane position should help you see and be seen, avoid blind spots, avoid hazards, protect your lane, show your intentions, avoid wind blasts, and give you an escape route. It should never help you avoid being seen.
